cd.label: CD — Claude desktop app, local Claude Code session in a fresh clone
cd.invocation:
In the Claude desktop app (Code tab) open a new session on the run's clone, set the model to Opus 5.5, the effort to high and the permission mode to Auto, and confirm all three before sending. Run `trialctl start {RUN_ID}` with the usage readings, then send exactly:

```
/prime-directive "Trial run {RUN_ID}: follow {MISSION} exactly"
```

Press Enter once, then keep your hands off the session: Escape and the Stop button interrupt the turn. Within ten minutes run `trialctl verify-start {RUN_ID}`; if it prints STOP, stop the run and record a setup incident.

cy-claude.label: CY — Chroxy dashboard session, Claude (SDK) provider
cy-claude.invocation:
In the Chroxy dashboard: New Session → provider Claude (SDK) → worktree isolation off (the clone is already isolated) → working directory = the run's clone → Create. A new session starts on the dashboard's default model, so set the model first: pick the Opus 5.5 entry in the header, and set the permission mode to Auto. Then run `trialctl preflight {RUN_ID} --phase session --session <the new session's id>`, which reads both changes from the daemon log, and `trialctl start {RUN_ID}` with the usage readings. Effort comes from `~/.claude/settings.json` (`modelSettings.claude-opus-5-5.effortLevel`), which the pre-send preflight checked; leave the header's thinking level at Auto. Send exactly:

```
/prime-directive "Trial run {RUN_ID}: follow {MISSION} exactly"
```

Press Enter once, then keep your hands off that session: Escape in the composer, Cmd+. and the Stop button all interrupt the turn. If the slash command is not recognised, send `Invoke the prime-directive skill with the argument: Trial run {RUN_ID}: follow {MISSION} exactly` and note "invocation: natural-language skill call". Within ten minutes run `trialctl verify-start {RUN_ID}`; if it prints STOP, stop the run and record a setup incident.

cx.label: CX — Codex desktop app in a fresh clone
cx.invocation:
In the Codex desktop app open the run's clone, set the model to gpt-6-astra and reasoning to extra-high, and approvals to the automatic reviewer ("Approve for me") with the default workspace-write sandbox, the setting October's B1-cx observed and the same sandbox the Chroxy Codex runs use. Run `trialctl start {RUN_ID}` with the usage readings, then send exactly:

```
/prompts:prime-directive Trial run {RUN_ID}: follow {MISSION} exactly
```

If `/prompts:` does not expand, Codex reads `~/.codex/prompts/prime-directive.md` itself; record the invocation method. Within ten minutes run `trialctl verify-start {RUN_ID}`; if it prints STOP, stop the run and record a setup incident.

cy-codex.label: CY — Chroxy dashboard session, Codex app-server provider (ChatGPT connection)
cy-codex.invocation:
In the Chroxy dashboard: New Session → provider Codex → connection ChatGPT subscription → working directory = the run's clone → Advanced: permission mode Auto, sandbox on the `Default` option (workspace-write), worktree isolation off → Create. Set the header to model gpt-6-astra and reasoning effort xhigh and confirm both (the header may show the config default first). Then run `trialctl preflight {RUN_ID} --phase session --session <the new session's id>` and `trialctl start {RUN_ID}` with the usage readings. Send exactly:

```
/prompts:prime-directive Trial run {RUN_ID}: follow {MISSION} exactly
```

If the session does not expand `/prompts:`, paste the full contents of `~/.codex/prompts/prime-directive.md` followed by the line `Trial run {RUN_ID}: follow {MISSION} exactly`, and note "invocation: pasted prompt". Press Enter once and keep your hands off that session. The daemon must not be restarted while the run is live (#8744). Within ten minutes run `trialctl verify-start {RUN_ID}`; if it prints STOP, stop the run and record a setup incident.
